resale_co.name: Housing Resale Certificate of Inspection (Housing Resale CO)
resale_co.issued_by: Pennsauken Township Department of Housing / Property Maintenance
resale_co.lead_time: No fixed number of days published. The township says to leave enough time between the inspection and settlement so the certificate is issued before settlement. If the home fails, the report arrives about 2 to 3 days after the inspection.
requirements: Interior and exterior housing resale inspection of every 1 and 2 family dwelling
Grading and drainage, sidewalks and driveways, accessory structures
Stumps from trees that caused sidewalk damage
Exterior structure: protective treatment, structural members, foundation walls, roofs and drainage
Roof certification and chimney certification (wood burning or gas) may be required
Stairways, decks, porches and balconies; handrails and guards
Interior structural members, surfaces, stairs and walking surfaces
Infestation / termite
Plumbing system hazards and plumbing certification
Mechanical appliances and mechanical certification

Electrical hazards and electrical certification; 2 outlets in every bedroom; protected outlets for sump or toilet pumps, bathrooms, kitchen counters and sinks within 6 feet; outdoor outlets weather resistant with a weatherproof cover
Smoke alarms, carbon monoxide detector, interior locked doors
Shed letter if there is a shed; grass or weeds
Rental registration if the property will be rented
New or open permits must be closed; no new occupancy until the final CO is issued

fees.label: Housing Resale CO plus Fire Certificate, combined application fee
fees.quote: The fee is $175.00 ($100 for the Housing Resale Certificate of Inspection & $75 for the Fire Certificate).

fees.label: Housing Resale Certificate of Inspection portion
fees.quote: The fee is $175.00 ($100 for the Housing Resale Certificate of Inspection & $75 for the Fire Certificate).

resale_co.how_to_apply: Complete the Housing Resale & Fire Certificate Inspection application (PDF) or apply online through the township's GovPilot portal. Submit the form with the $175 fee (cash, check or money order payable to Pennsauken Township) to the Municipal Building, Attn: Housing / Property Maintenance Dept., 5605 N. Crescent Blvd., Pennsauken, NJ 08110. The inspection is scheduled once the form and fee are received. Housing & Property Maintenance Assistant Suzanne Paul (ext. 1411, spaul@pennsauken.gov) handles applications and scheduling.

evidence.quote: A housing resale CO and fire certificate is required for every transfer of ownership for all one and/or two-family dwellings.
To obtain the CO and fire certificate the property must pass a housing resale inspection.
Housing & Property Maintenance Assistant Email Suzanne Paul Phone: 856-665-1000 Ext. 1411
Manager Housing / Property Maintenance Email Will Rivera Phone: 856-665-1000 Ext. 1410

By Township Ordinance all one and/or two-family dwellings are required to have a housing resale inspection completed for the interior and exterior of the property and obtain a Certificate of Inspection prior to settlement.
NOTE: The property must pass the housing inspection and all open permits must be closed before the Housing Resale Certificate of Inspection is issued.
Payment can be made by cash, check or money order payable to Pennsauken Township.

resale_co.notes: Online application portal (GovPilot): https://main.govpilot.com/web/public/76ff6888-efb_Rental-Resale-Township-of-Pennsauken?uid=7081&ust=NJ&pu=1&id=0 . A buyer (only the buyer) may request a notarized Affidavit for a Temporary CO to take responsibility for listed violations; if the report says no occupancy until final CO, the Temporary CO is issued 'For Work Only'. Required construction permits (including for work done without permits) must be obtained and pass inspection before the final certificate. The application and information PDFs are dated December 2024 and still list older contacts (ext. 133; Manager Patte Magro, ext. 145); the current department page lists Manager Will Rivera (ext. 1410, wrivera@pennsauken.gov), Housing & Property Maintenance Assistant Suzanne Paul (ext. 1411) and three Code Enforcement Inspectors (ext. 1412 to 1414). Rental program is separate: 1 and 2 family rentals register annually ($350) and pass a rental inspection; a township Lead Safe Visual Assessment for rentals costs $170. No reinspection fee for the housing resale inspection was found.

requirements: Each level must have an AC hard wired or 10-year sealed battery smoke alarm; all smoke alarms must be within 10 years of the manufacture date

Alarm type depends on original construction date: pre-1975 homes need 10-year sealed battery alarms on each level within 10 feet of each bedroom; newer homes need hard wired interconnected alarms per the era table
A smoke alarm is required in every bedroom regardless of the home's age, plus outside sleeping areas and on every level
Smoke alarm in the basement within 10 feet of the stairway (not in the stairway), and at the top of walk-up attic stairs
Carbon monoxide alarm within 10 feet of each sleeping area
Hard-wired proprietary fire alarm systems must be tested per NFPA 72 with a test report at inspection

evidence.quote: The housing resale and fire inspections are completed by the township housing department inspectors.
All smoke alarms shall be within 10 years of the manufacture date.
A smoke alarm is required to be installed in every bedroom.

Before any R-3 or R-4 residential unit is sold, leased or otherwise subject to change of occupancy for residential purposes, the owner shall obtain a certificate of smoke detector and carbon monoxide alarm compliance (CSDCMAC)
If the change of occupancy specified in the application for a CSDC does not occur within six months, a new application shall be required.
Smoke detectors required to be installed in accordance with N.J.A.C. 5:70-4.19 must be installed prior to the scheduled inspection.

fire_cert.notes: In practice the resale fire certificate is handled by the Housing / Property Maintenance Department together with the resale CO, for a flat $75 inside the $175 combined fee. Town code Chapter 243, Article V (Ord. 2017:09, read through the ecode360 print view) still sets a tiered CSDCMAC fee ($50 / $85 / $140) and a $50 reinspection fee and names the Bureau of Fire Prevention; the code tiers are listed for reference, but the township's current application charges the flat $75. The NJ DCA fire directory lists the Pennsauken Construction Office (856-665-1000) for smoke detector compliance; Fire Official Steven Schwegel, Jr. (sschwegel@pennsaukenfire.org, 856-665-0774) runs the Fire Marshal Office, 2215 Merchantville Ave, which handles fire code permits and inspections. The township's smoke/CO instruction PDF is titled to include fire extinguishers but gives no extinguisher rules, in line with the 2025 state change (P.L.2025, c.19).

other_items.label: Open and required construction permits must be closed
other_items.detail: All permits must be obtained, inspected and pass inspection before the final Certificate of Inspection is issued. Construction dept: 856-665-1000 x129, building@pennsauken.gov.

other_items.label: Temporary CO by buyer affidavit
other_items.detail: Only the buyer may sign a notarized Affidavit for a Temporary CO, accepting responsibility for the violations; it must be delivered to Housing before settlement.

other_items.label: Rental registration if buyer will rent
other_items.detail: Checklist item 251.19 rental registration required; 1-2 family rentals register annually ($350) and are inspected.

open_questions: Does the town code tier schedule for the CSDCMAC ($50 / $85 / $140) still apply in any case, or is the flat $75 on the combined application the only fire certificate fee?
Is there a reinspection fee for a failed housing resale inspection (code sets $50 for a failed smoke/CO inspection only)?
No published minimum lead time or validity period for the housing resale certificate.
Which form and fee applies to a 2-family resale (application does not separate 1 and 2 family)?
